questions.q: Why does this lesson say repeated logic without functions/methods is a problem?
options: Apex physically cannot run the same logic more than once without a method
If logic needs to change later, every copied instance has to be found and fixed, and missing even one leaves a hidden bug
Repeated logic always runs slower than logic inside a method
Methods are required by the Apex compiler for any program to run at all
questions.explain: The lesson's framing is that copied logic becomes a maintenance risk: when it needs to change, every copy must be found and updated, and a missed copy becomes a hidden bug -- which is exactly the problem a reusable method solves.

questions.q: What is the precise difference between a parameter and an argument, per this lesson?
options: A parameter is the named placeholder in a method's own definition; an argument is the actual value supplied when the method is called
A parameter is the return value, and an argument is the method's name
They are two different words for exactly the same thing with no distinction
An argument is used only in Apex, and a parameter is used only in other languages
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly distinguishes the two: subtotal and taxRate are parameters (the blueprint in the method's definition), while 100 and 0.08 are arguments (the real values supplied at a specific call).

questions.q: What does a `void` return type mean for an Apex method?
options: The method must always throw an exception
The method returns the number zero by default
The method hands back no value at all -- it simply does something and finishes, with no return statement carrying a value
The method can never be called more than once
questions.explain: The lesson's logOrderSummary example declares void as its return type specifically because it only performs an action (a debug log) and doesn't hand any value back to the caller.

questions.q: What happens to a variable declared inside a method once that method finishes running?
options: It becomes a global variable accessible from any other method
It is gone -- only the value returned (if any) survives past that point, since the variable's scope was limited to that method call
It is automatically saved to the Salesforce database
It keeps its value permanently and can be reused the next time the method is called
questions.explain: The lesson explains that a variable's scope ends when the method finishes: everything declared inside it, including parameters, ceases to exist once the method call ends, and only a returned value (if any) persists.

questions.q: Why can two different methods both have a variable named `total` with no conflict, per this lesson's explanation of scope?
options: Because Apex automatically renames duplicate variable names behind the scenes
Because each method's `total` only exists within that specific method's own call, and is invisible to code outside it, including other methods
Because Apex does not allow two methods to use the same variable name, so this scenario is actually impossible
Because variables named `total` are a reserved special case in Apex
questions.explain: The lesson states that scope confines a variable to the region of code where it was declared -- so two methods can each declare their own `total` with zero conflict, since neither method's variable is visible to the other.
